BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC                                   )
 SERVICE COMPANY’S APPLICATION FOR: (1)                                 )
 REVISION OF ITS RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE                              )   Docket 25-00079-UT
 NOTICE 341; AND (2) OTHER ASSOCIATED RELIEF                            )


                          ORDER UPDATING PROTECTIVE ORDER

THIS MATTER comes before Keven Gedko and Patrick Schaefer, hearing examiners for the

New Mexico Public Regulation Commission, upon their own Motion, to update and clarify the

policies and procedures outlined in the protective order issued on February 24, 2026, to incorporate

new requirements for filing and accessing confidential documents in the Commission’s PRCe360

Docketing System. The Hearing Examiner FINDS and CONCLUDES as follows:

        1.      On January 26, 2026, the Commission's new electronic case management system,

PRCe360, went live.

        2.      With the advent of the new docketing system, certain procedures for (1) filing

confidential documents into the record and (2) executing confidentiality agreements have

changed.

        3.      In light of these changes, the procedural order on record in this matter does not

contain the proper procedures for filing and accessing confidential documents in the PRCe360

system and must be updated.

    IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

        A.      This Protective Order shall be used in place of the existing protective order for the further

duration of this Docket. The attached Protective Order is substantially the same as the existing protective

order, with the exception of paragraphs E and F, which provide updated instruction for filing and accessing

confidential documents in the PRCe360 Docketing System.
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       B.      This Order establishes a procedure for the handling of information that a party

claims is confidential material. This Order shall not be construed as a ruling on the confidentiality

of any document or information.

       C.      Consistent with IPRA and the statutory limits on the Commission’s authority to

issue protective orders, parties SHALL ONLY seek protection of material that is protectable under

statute and regulation, SHALL NOT designate documents as confidential that are not entitled to

protection, and SHALL NOT make blanket assertions that all documents or entire subsets of

documents in this case are subject to protection.

       D.      Designating Information as Confidential

       1.      This Order provides protection for confidential and proprietary information

identified and clearly designated by parties as “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL.”

       2.      Material may only be designated as confidential if the disclosing party can establish

that the material is not in the public domain and is protected by applicable law, including IPRA

and the New Mexico Trade Secrets Act. 1 No material shall be treated as confidential material if

it: (a) is in the public domain at the time of disclosure; (b) becomes part of the public domain

through no fault of a party who received it under this order; (c) is in the lawful possession of the

receiving party at the time it is disclosed under this order; (d) is or has been received by a party on

a nonrestricted basis from a third party that has the right to make such a disclosure; or (e) has been

or becomes disclosed as non-confidential material in any other legal or regulatory proceeding.

       3.      All material submitted to the Commission as provided below or furnished to other

parties pursuant to any request for information, subpoena, or other mode of discovery that is




1 NMSA 1978, § 57-3A-2 (2025).


                                                 -2-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


claimed to be of a trade secret, proprietary or confidential nature, and protectable under IPRA shall

be clearly designated “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL” by the party claiming protection.

       4.      If a document contains both confidential and non-confidential information, the

party claiming confidentiality shall claim protection only for the portions of the document that

satisfy the standards for confidential treatment and clearly identify the specific portions of the

document for which confidentiality is claimed.

       E.      Segregation of Files

       1.      Access to and review of confidential material shall be strictly controlled by the

terms of this Order.

       2.      Any document containing confidential material should be watermarked or

otherwise clearly reflect that it contains confidential material.

       3.      Confidential material provided IN RESPONSE TO DISCOVERY REQUESTS

SHALL NOT be “filed” with the Commission.

       4.      Confidential material to be filed with the Commission shall be marked

CONFIDENTIAL and filed electronically in the Commission’s PRCe360 Docket System as

confidential. Instructions on how to file confidential documents in the Commissions PRCe360

Docketing System are available on the Commission website, or if assistance is required please

email prc.support@prc.nm.gov, or call 505-637-2640.

       5.      Confidential material filed with the Commission shall be e-mailed to the Hearing

Examiners and the subject line and text of the e-mail shall make clear that the message is intended

to transmit confidential material in this docket. The materials will be withheld from inspection by

any person except under the conditions established in this order unless the parties agree the




                                                 -3-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


material may be released for public review or, after notice to the parties and hearing, by order of

the Commission and/or a court with jurisdiction to order public disclosure.

       F.      Confidentiality Agreement

       No access to confidential material shall be authorized under the terms of this Order until

the person requesting access to the material does one, or both, of the following:

       1.      Creates an account, or accesses an existing account, on the Commission’s PRCe360

Docketing System and executes an electronic confidentiality agreement for this docket number.

Instructions on how to execute an electronic confidentiality agreement are available on the

Commission website, or if assistance is required or if assistance is required please email

prc.support@prc.nm.gov, or call 505-637-2640.

       2.      Signs a confidentiality agreement in the form attached to this order as Attachment

A. The executed confidentiality agreement shall be filed with the Commission and served on the

parties as required by 1.2.2.10 NMAC and applicable orders in this case prior to inspection of the

confidential material.

       Commissioners and their advisory staff and expert consultants, Commission’s Records

Management Bureau, Commission’s General Counsel and Staff, hearing examiners and Staff, and

court reporter, are not required to sign the confidentiality agreement to view confidential material.

       G.       Availability to the Commission and Parties

       Except as otherwise provided in this order, the only persons permitted access to the

confidential material (other than the individuals identified in the preceding paragraph) are parties

to this case and their employees and legal counsel who have executed one, or both, of the above

described the confidentiality agreements.

       H.      Availability to Non-Signatories


                                                -4-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


         All persons who receive service of filings in this case and who have not executed the

confidentiality agreement shall receive, on the date that they are filed, the affidavits required under

Paragraphs L(1)(e) and L(2)(b) and all non-confidential portions of any documents marked as

confidential material in redacted form.

         I.     Preservation of Confidentiality

         Persons provided access to confidential material by operation of this Order shall not use or

disclose the confidential material for purposes of business or competition or any other purpose

other than the purpose of preparation for and adjudication of this proceeding (except as provided

in Paragraph P) and any appeals arising from this proceeding. Confidential material shall be used

only as contemplated here and parties shall take all reasonable precautions to keep the confidential

material secure. The contents of the confidential material shall not be disclosed to anyone other

than persons who have executed the confidentiality agreement.

         J.     Challenges to Claims of Confidentiality

         A party may at any time challenge a claim that materials identified as confidential should,

in fact, be given confidential status. In the event of such a challenge, the following procedures

apply:

         1.     The party asserting the challenge shall contact counsel for the party holding the

allegedly confidential materials and attempt to resolve any differences informally.

         2.     If the parties cannot resolve the disagreement informally, then the party challenging

the claim of confidentiality shall file a motion with the Commission for a ruling on the challenge

(a process referred to as a “request for confidentiality determination”).

         3.     When a request for confidentiality determination is filed and served, the owner or

holder of the material held out as confidential shall, within three business days of service of the


                                                 -5-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


request for confidentiality determination, e-mail the materials to the Hearing Examiners for in-

camera inspection. The documents should comply with the formatting requirements described in

Paragraph E of this document.

       4.      The holder of the materials held out as confidential shall, without order or action

by the Commission and within five business days after service of a request for confidentiality

determination, file an initial brief and supporting affidavit stating in detail the basis for the claim

of confidentiality and may request a hearing on the matter. Failure to file an initial brief and

supporting affidavit shall be deemed a waiver of the confidentiality claim.

       5.      Within five business days after service of the initial brief and supporting affidavit,

the party that filed the request for confidentiality determination shall file a response brief and

supporting responsive affidavit.

       6.      Within three business days of service of the response brief and supporting affidavit,

the holder of the purportedly confidential material may file a reply brief.

       7.      Any other party may brief its position by filing a brief opposing the claim of

confidentiality five business days after service of the initial brief or supporting confidentiality and

non-disclosure by filing a brief within three business days after service of the response of the party

that filed the request for confidentiality determination.

       8.      The burden of proof to show the confidentiality of the materials held out as

confidential rests with the party claiming confidentiality.

       9.      The parties shall not make public any information regarding materials held out as

confidential until the Commission rules on the claim of confidentiality. Following a Commission

ruling on confidentiality, the information shall be made available only pursuant to the

Commission’s order(s).


                                                 -6-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       K.      Requests Not to Disclose to Persons Executing a Confidentiality Agreement

       If any party possessing confidential materials wishes to decline to provide those materials

to specific parties who have signed confidentiality agreements, then the party possessing the

materials must file a pleading with the Commission prior to the time the material is due to be

produced explaining the reasons why the materials should not be provided. The party denied

access to the confidential materials may then file a response within five business days of service

of the possessor’s pleading. The party seeking to preclude parties from receiving confidential

materials shall have the burden of proof. Confidential material shall not be produced to the

challenged party until a ruling by the Hearing Examiner.

       L.      Use of Confidential Materials and Bench Requests

       1.      Use by Staff and parties.

       If any party other than the party asserting the claim of confidentiality intends to use

confidential material or material over which a claim of confidentiality is made in this proceeding

in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) or at the hearing, and even if the party using the

confidential material does not intend to challenge the claim of confidentiality, then the following

procedures shall apply:

               a.      The party intending to use the confidential material shall inform the party

       asserting the claim of confidentiality of the intent and manner of use as follows: (i) for use

       in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on the date the testimony is

       filed, and (ii) for use at the hearing, notice to be provided to the Hearing Examiners, parties,

       and Staff as early as is feasible and preferably to be filed before the start of the hearing

       unless otherwise ordered or approved.




                                                -7-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


                 b.   Within three business days of receiving notice of the intent to use

      confidential material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days of receiving notice

      of the intent to use confidential material at the hearing, the party claiming confidentiality

      shall state whether it objects to public disclosure of the confidential material. If the party

      asserting confidentiality fails to make this statement, its objection to disclosure shall be

      waived.

                 c.   Pending a ruling on confidentiality, any party using confidential material in

      pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) shall, on the date that the notice is filed: (i) file a

      public version with the Confidential Material redacted; (ii) file a confidential version in

      accordance with the procedures in Paragraph E; and (iii) serve the confidential version on

      parties who have executed a confidentiality agreement and to the Hearing Examiners.

              d.      If the party asserting the confidentiality of material objects to public

      disclosure of the material, it shall file a request seeking confidential treatment of the

      material within three business days after it receives notice of the intended use of the

      material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days after it receives notice of the

      intended use of the material at the hearing.

                 e.   Any request filed pursuant to Paragraph L(1)(d) shall include:

            i.        An affidavit consistent with 1.2.2.8.B(1) NMAC that satisfies the

      claimant’s burden of making a prima facie showing that protection is appropriate for the

      information claimed to be confidential material and that includes (at a minimum) the

      following information with respect to each document marked confidential:

      (1)    the date that the material was prepared;

      (2)    the author of the material;


                                               -8-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       (3)         a list of all persons (other than the disclosing party and its representatives) in

       possession of the material;

       (4)         a description of the subject matter of the material and the contents of the material;

       (6)         the number of pages of material;

       (7)         how the material was acquired; and

       (8)      the basis for all claims of confidentiality, including a showing that each document

       marked confidential comes within one or more of the exceptions to the general disclosure

       requirement of IPRA.

             ii.          A brief that sets forth the legal basis for protection and states whether the

       public interest requires that the material be used and whether an abstract of or the extraction

       of specific information from the material can be used as an alternative.

                f.        The party asserting the confidentiality of the material shall e-mail the

       Hearing Examiners the confidential materials for in-camera inspection.

               g.         Within seven days of the filing of a request under Paragraph L(1)(d), the

       party seeking to use the confidential material shall file a response addressing the legal and

       factual merits of each confidentiality claim, including Staff’s or the party’s position on

       whether the confidential material is in fact confidential. Any factual assertions in the

       response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

       2.       Use by party asserting confidentiality.

       If any party asserting the confidentiality of material intends to use the material in this

proceeding in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) or at the hearing, then the following

procedures apply:




                                                   -9-
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


              a.      The party shall file a notice of intent that describes the manner of use and

       requesting confidential treatment of its use of the material as follows: (i) for use in pre-

       filed testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on the date the testimony is filed;

       and (ii) for use at the hearing, notice to be provided to the Hearing Examiners, parties, and

       Staff as early as is feasible and preferably before the start of the hearing. Pending a ruling

       on confidentiality, the party using confidential material in pre-filed testimony (including

       exhibits) shall, on the date that the notice is filed: (i) file a public version with the

       confidential material redacted; (ii) file a confidential version under seal in accordance with

       the procedure in Paragraph E; and (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have

       executed a confidentiality agreement and the Hearing Examiners.

              b.      Such party shall file a request seeking confidential treatment of the material

       on the date that the notice required under Paragraph L(2)(a) is filed. This request shall

       include the affidavit and brief described in Paragraph L(1)(e).

              c.      Within seven days of filing a request under Paragraph L(2)(b), or as

       otherwise ordered, Staff shall, and any other intervener may file a response addressing the

       legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim including Staff’s or the party’s

       position on whether the material is in fact confidential. Any factual assertions in the

       response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

       3.     Bench requests

       If the Hearing Examiners or Commission require a party to file a document and the party

objects to public disclosure of the document or portions of the document on confidentiality

grounds, then the following procedures apply:




                                               - 10 -
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


             a.      On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall (i) file a

      public version of the document with the confidential material redacted; (ii) file a

      confidential version of the document in accordance with the procedure in Paragraph E; and

      (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have signed the confidentiality agreement

      and the Hearing Examiners.

             b.      On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall file a

      request seeking confidential treatment of the material, including the affidavit and brief

      described in Paragraph L(1)(e).

             c.      Within seven days of the filing of the request seeking confidential treatment

      of the material, or as otherwise ordered, Staff shall, and any intervenor may, file a response

      addressing the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim including Staff’s or

      the party’s position on whether the material is in fact confidential. Any factual assertions

      in the response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

      4.     Rulings

             a.      The Commission shall evaluate the materiality and relevance of the

      confidential material to this case and, if necessary, determine if claimed confidential

      material contains confidential or proprietary information and, if so, determine whether the

      public interest requires that the confidential or proprietary information be produced at the

      hearing in this case, whether an abstract of or the extraction of specific information from

      the confidential or proprietary information should be produced for use at the hearing, or

      whether the confidential material shall be admitted and treated as a confidential exhibit.

             b.      The Commission may issue a ruling on the requests under this paragraph

      based upon the affidavits and/or a hearing or other procedure as determined by the


                                              - 11 -
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       Commission. The confidential material shall remain confidential pending a ruling by the

       Commission. Following a Commission ruling on confidentiality, the information shall be

       available only as provided by Commission order.

               c.      Following a Commission ruling on confidentiality or privilege, the

       information shall be made available only pursuant to the Commission’s order; provided

       however that an application for reconsideration, rehearing or interlocutory appeal filed by

       any holder of confidential material shall act as a stay of such order pending reconsideration,

       rehearing or interlocutory appeal.

       5.      Hearings involving confidential material

       During this proceeding, those portions of any hearings where confidential material

obtained pursuant to the terms of this order are likely to be disclosed shall be conducted in a manner

that the Commission determines is consistent with the Open Meetings Act, IPRA, the Public Utility

Act, and other relevant statutes.

       6.      Admissibility

       The parties retain the right to object to the admission into evidence of any confidential

material on any proper grounds including relevance or materiality.

       M.      Filing and Delivery Pursuant to Commission Electronic Filing Policy

       Whenever the terms of this order require a filing of pleadings or materials, such filings are

subject to the Commission’s Electronic Filing Policy then in effect. Service of the filed documents

shall be made to parties having filed confidentiality agreements by emailing scanned versions of

the materials reflecting the formatting identified in ordering Paragraph E. To the extent that this

Order requires delivery of any materials to the Commission in connection with a request for

confidentiality determination, delivery to the Hearing Examiners will be by email as an attachment


                                                - 12 -
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


or as electronic file transfer. The email delivering the document shall briefly describe the materials

and reflect the formatting directions at ordering Paragraph E but shall not include any commentary

or argument. Notice of the delivery of materials to the Hearing Examiners will be provided to all

parties and individuals on the service list.

       N.      Appeal

       Sealed portions of the record in the proceeding may be forwarded to any court of competent

jurisdiction for purposes of an appeal.

       O.       Continuation of Protection

       Disclosure of confidential material is limited by this Order for two years from the date of

the final order or final decision on appeal whichever is later, provided that the Commission may

extend the period of protection upon a motion of a party filed prior to expiration of the period of

protection.

       P.      Use in Other Commission Proceedings

       Nothing in this Order prohibits a person who executes a confidentiality agreement from

seeking to use confidential material in other Commission proceedings, subject to any applicable

rulings in such proceedings, and provided the original owner or holder of the material is served

with the notice of intent to use the material. The procedure set forth in Paragraph L(1) shall apply.

       Q.      For purposes of this Order, “Commission” means presiding officer, hearing

examiner, or the Commissioners.

       R.      The provisions of 1.2.2.8(B) NMAC governing the procedures to be used when any

person desires to protect documents or information from disclosure are waived pursuant to

1.2.2.8(D) NMAC.




                                                - 13 -
                  BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Updating Protective Order                              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       S.      Any person executing a confidentiality agreement consents to the jurisdiction of the

Commission and the New Mexico courts for resolution of disputes regarding alleged violations of

this Order. Pursuant to 1.2.2.8 NMAC, sanctions may be imposed under applicable laws for

violation of this Order.

       T.      This Order is effective immediately.

       U.      A copy of this Order shall be served on all persons on the official service list.

       ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on April 17, 2026.
